subject: Proposal: response-lane credits + canary fallback rights
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan@acmehealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Response lanes, credits and canary fallback - initial ask

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme Health liked the latency profiles and the tooling around rollouts. Before we get legal and procurement moving, we need a clearer picture of how Redwood would package an SLA + premium-support contract for a mid-size healthcare deployment. A few specific asks: 

- A high-level matrix that maps uptime bands to crediting (we run regulatory workloads so availability matters).
- Example response lanes (P1/P2) and corresponding target response times for on-call and priority routing.
- Whether Redwood will allow a controlled "canary fallback" to a lower-cost model variant during regional pressure, and if so how credits or penalties apply.
- Pricing sketch for an annualized, prepaid retainer that bundles credits (we're exploring prepay vs monthly usage).

We expect to start procurement conversations in mid-December; procurement will want a PO-ready quote and the legal team will want the exact crediting language. Can you send the SLA tier matrix + a short note on the canary fallback policy?

Appreciate it — cc'd Marissa from our integrations team so she can confirm ops constraints.

Jordan Ellis
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Health
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Response lanes, credits and canary fallback - initial ask

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Attached is a draft "SLA_Tier_Matrix.xlsx" that maps availability bands to token-based credit schedules and example response lanes. High level summary here: 

- Availability bands (examples): 99.9% / 99.95% / 99.99%. Credits are expressed as % of monthly invoice and scale by minutes of downtime within a billing period.
- Response lanes (ops): P1 (service down, safety-impacting) = 1 hour initial response, 4 hour mitigation target; P2 (degraded) = 4 hour initial response; P3 = next-business-day.
- Retainer model: we offer an annual prepaid bucket that pre-purchases "response credits" and priority capacity. Example: a 12-month retainer that buys 50% reserved capacity at x% discount vs on-demand and includes a pool of credits to offset small outages without a formal SLA claim.
- Canary fallback: supported. In practice we route traffic to a quantized-compatible model variant when regional capacity spikes. Fallbacks are surfaced in Console, and if fallbacks are initiated for >2% of monthly token volume they reduce next-billing-period retainer credits by a small step (we track minutes and apply a capped offset). We can draft exact wording; legal tends to prefer a cap and an exclusion for scheduled maintenance.

Numbers (illustrative):
- 12-month prepaid retainer: $180k annual retainer (reserved capacity) -> includes 2,500 credit units and 20% off on extra capacity.
- Crediting example: 99.9% -> 5% invoice credit per major incident (capped monthly).

Next steps I propose: 1) Marissa and I iterate the credit caps and the on-call windows; 2) we put together a PO-ready quote and a DocuSign-ready addendum with the canary fallback clause; 3) if helpful we set a short call with engineering to lock in on the fallback behavior.

I've attached the matrix (SLA_Tier_Matrix.xlsx) and a one-pager. Let me know a good time next week to sync.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan@acmehealth.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 14:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Response lanes, credits and canary fallback - ops + procurement notes

Looping in Karthik from Pricing/Packaging to confirm discount scaffolding. Operational notes for Acme: 

- Escalation rights: for an annual retainer we include a named escalation contact and a tiered incident playbook; on-call rotation is 24/7 for P1s and business-hours for P2s.
- Credit caps: standard practice is a monthly cap equal to 100% of the monthly portion of the retainer for single-account incidents; we can lower it for enterprise deals but that reduces available discount.
- Canary fallbacks: engineering will want a bounded SLA clause — our suggested language is fallback allowed for <72 hours per quarter per region without penalty, beyond that the credit schedule applies. Can add exclusions for force majeure.
- Procurement docs: attached is our current quote (proposed_retainer_quote_v3.pdf) that Nikhil used for pricing examples. Please confirm the billing contact and preferred PO cadence (annual vs quarterly).

Jordan — if you can share procurement contact and the target start date (you mentioned Jan 1 in the call), Karthik and I will produce a PO-ready statement of work and a DocuSign envelope. If Acme wants a hard cap on credits (hard cap preferred by your finance team), tell us the cap and we will model pricing with that constraint.

Marissa Cole
Head, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan@acmehealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Response lanes, credits and canary fallback - ops + procurement notes

Thanks — and appreciated the clear examples. A few quick confirmations from Acme: 

- We are interested in the 12-month prepaid retainer but need a hard monthly credit cap for finance. Proposed cap: credits not to exceed 50% of the monthly amortized retainer in any billing period. If that cap increases cost materially, flag it and we'll iterate.
- Canary fallback: we accept the bounded fallback approach (<=72 hours per quarter per region) with the exclusion language. We also want an SLA-visible toggle in the Console so our SREs can see when traffic switches to the fallback model.
- Target legal sign date: we are aiming to sign the retainer addendum the week of Dec 13. Procurement will issue PO upon DocuSign signature. Attached is a placeholder PO (PO_Acme_98765.pdf) to accelerate internal routing; it's not the final dollar amount yet.

Please produce a final PoA (price on agreement) that reflects the credit cap above and the Console-visible fallback flag. If you can get a DocuSign starter envelope over by next Wed (Dec 2) that will keep us on track.

On the fallback point, quoting Nikhil: "fallbacks are surfaced in Console" — that visibility is a must for our compliance team.

Jordan Ellis
Director, Platform Engineering, Acme Health
